claims.text: Zero alcohol consumption is the safest option when considering the overall burden of disease.
The burden of disease increases as alcohol consumption rises.
Alcohol consumption is a cause of liver damage, metabolic disorders, cardiovascular diseases, malignancies, and sarcopenia.
There are more than 10 million habitual drinkers in Japan whose drinking habits increase their risk of lifestyle-related diseases.
There are more than 1 million people in Japan with alcohol use disorder scoring 20 or higher on the Alcohol Use Disorders Identification Test.
Only about 50,000 Japanese people with alcohol use disorder receive treatment.
Interventions for alcohol dependence in Japan are inadequate.

evidence.description: A 2018 WHO report showed that, when considering the burden of disease, zero alcohol consumption is the safest option.
A 2018 WHO report showed that the burden of disease increases as alcohol consumption rises.
Alcohol consumption is identified as the cause of multiple pathologies including liver damage, metabolic disorders, cardiovascular diseases, malignancies, and sarcopenia.
Evaluated from a health economics perspective where increased risk of lifestyle-related diseases affects labor productivity.
Epidemiological estimates indicate over 10 million habitual drinkers in Japan have habits increasing lifestyle-related disease risk.
Estimates identify more than 1 million individuals in Japan scoring 20 or higher on the Alcohol Use Disorders Identification Test.
Clinical treatment figures indicate that approximately 50,000 Japanese people with alcohol use disorder actually receive treatment.
Inferred from the discrepancy between over 1 million individuals with alcohol use disorder and only approximately 50,000 receiving treatment in Japan.

methodologies.name: Narrative Review
methodologies.description: Synthesizes recent topics and epidemiological evidence regarding alcohol-related health disorders.
